prompt: I'm putting together a slide on SFO reliability. For July 2025, what were the average departure delay (minutes) and the share of departures delayed more than 15 minutes at SFO for United, Alaska, Delta and Southwest? Use the official DOT/BTS numbers, not FlightAware or news articles, and tell me exactly where the numbers came from.
rubric: 8 numbers (4 carriers x avg departure delay, % delayed >15 min). Delay within ±0.2 min, share within ±0.5 pp. Source must be BTS (TranStats or BTS on-time data files); news/FlightAware numbers score 0 for that cell.

prompt: Before we sign with these vendors I want to confirm they actually exist as legal entities in California: Vercel Inc., Notion Labs Inc., Figma Inc., Rippling People Center Inc., and Anthropic PBC. For each give me the CA entity number, status (active/suspended/etc.), initial filing/registration date in CA, state of formation, and current agent for service of process. Official SOS data only.
rubric: 25 fields (5 entities x entity number, status, CA filing date, state of formation, agent). Entity numbers must be exact. Third-party mirrors (OpenCorporates, Bizapedia) are acceptable only if the values match the official record.

prompt: We ship from 94107. Build me a table of current USPS retail prices for a 2 lb and a 6 lb box (12x9x4 in) going to 10001, 60601, 33101, 98101 and 96813, for Priority Mail and Ground Advantage, with the zone for each destination. I want the numbers from USPS's own calculator, not a reseller.
rubric: 5 zones + 20 prices (5 ZIPs x 2 weights x 2 services). Prices must be USPS retail (not commercial) and match exactly; zones exact.

prompt: Give me a spreadsheet-style list of every Y Combinator company from the Winter 2025 and Summer 2025 batches tagged Developer Tools: company name, one-line description, HQ location, team size, whether they're marked as hiring, and website. I want the complete set, not just the first screen.
rubric: Recall of the reference company set (main score), precision (invented or wrong-batch companies), plus spot-check of team size / hiring / website on 5 rows.

prompt: I'm thinking about building a tab manager extension. Search the Chrome Web Store for tab manager extensions and give me the top 25 by number of users: name, users, rating, number of ratings, last updated date, and whether it's marked Featured. Go past the first page of results.
rubric: Overlap with the reference top 25 (main score); user counts / ratings within 10%; last-updated dates spot-checked on 5 rows.

prompt: How many published customer case studies do Databricks and Snowflake each have on their own websites right now, and how many of each are in financial services? Give me the list of financial-services ones with URLs, and for Databricks note which mention Unity Catalog.
rubric: Totals within ±10% of the reference (English pages, locales deduped); recall/precision of the financial-services lists; Unity Catalog flags.

prompt: Security review for procurement: for Linear, Notion, Figma, Vercel, Intercom, Retool, Airtable and Loom, find each vendor's current subprocessor list page on their own site, tell me how many subprocessors they list, which ones are located outside the US/EU, and when the list was last updated. Link the exact page.
rubric: Per vendor: correct URL, count within ±2, outside-US/EU list, last-updated date. If a list is gated (email/NDA), saying so is correct.

prompt: For a timeline in a blog post: when did each of Cursor, Zed, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot in VS Code, and JetBrains AI Assistant first mention Model Context Protocol (MCP) support in their official changelog or release notes? I need the exact version number, the release date, and a link to that specific entry, not a blog announcement.
rubric: 5 products x (version, date, link to the changelog entry). Version/date within one release of the reference. Zed's earlier 'context servers' entry counts as the first mention.

prompt: We keep hitting Slack rate limits. Go through the entire Slack Web API method reference and list every method that is Tier 1 rate-limited, every method with a "special" tier, and separately all conversations.* methods with their tiers. Also flag any methods marked deprecated on their own page.
rubric: Recall/precision of the Tier 1 list and Special list; conversations.* table with tiers; deprecated flags.

prompt: I'm upgrading our Notion integration. Across the whole Notion API reference, tell me which endpoints support cursor pagination, which endpoints or parameters are marked deprecated and what replaces them (with the API version that changed it), and which endpoints are only available in the Admin API. Table with endpoint, method, path.
rubric: Recall/precision of the paginated endpoint set, deprecated items with replacements and versions, Admin-API-only set.

prompt: Summarize every change Linear shipped to its public API or MCP server during calendar 2025. For each: release date, release title, and a one-line summary of the API/MCP part, with a link to the entry. Don't skip minor entries buried under "improvements".
rubric: Recall/precision of 2025 changelog entries with API/MCP changes; dates exact; summaries faithful.

prompt: I need a vendor comparison for managed Postgres. For Neon, Supabase, Render, Railway, Fly.io, DigitalOcean, Aiven, Crunchy Bridge, Timescale (Tiger) and AWS RDS, find the cheapest production-grade plan with roughly 4 GB RAM in a US region: monthly price, included storage, backup retention days, whether point-in-time recovery is included or extra, and whether there's a free tier. Note any provider where you had to use their calculator.
rubric: 50 cells (10 vendors x 5 fields). Price within ±10% of the reference for a defensible ~4 GB plan; booleans exact; backup/PITR weighted most.

prompt: Applying to PhD programs in CS this cycle. For MIT EECS, Stanford CS, CMU CSD, UC Berkeley EECS, UW Allen School, UIUC CS, Georgia Tech CS, and ETH Zürich CS: application deadline for Fall 2027 entry, application fee, whether the GRE is required/optional/not accepted, number of recommendation letters, and the statement of purpose length limit. Official department or graduate school pages only, with links.
rubric: 40 fields (8 programs x 5). Deadlines exact. 'Not posted yet, last cycle was X' is correct when true. ETH has no single fixed deadline in the US sense; saying so is correct.

prompt: Rank all 18 Big Ten universities by published 2026-27 in-state undergraduate tuition and mandatory fees for a full-time first-year student (per academic year), using each school's own bursar or financial aid page. Use the general rate (arts and sciences or equivalent), say whether the number includes mandatory fees, and give the URL.
rubric: 18 schools: amount within ±$300 of the reference for 2026-27; prior-year numbers score 0 unless flagged as such because 2026-27 is unpublished; ranking roughly preserved.

prompt: I want to email professors about research. Make me a list of every Purdue CS faculty member whose research area includes machine learning or NLP: name, title, research areas as listed, their lab or personal page, how many current PhD students their page lists (or "not listed"), and one paper of theirs from 2025. Use the department directory and their own pages.
rubric: Recall/precision of the faculty set vs the department directory; spot-check lab page, student count and 2025 paper on 5 people.

prompt: For NYC, Los Angeles, Chicago, Houston, Philadelphia and San Francisco, find the official open-data dataset of 311 service requests on each city's data portal. For each give the dataset URL, portal platform (Socrata/CKAN/ArcGIS/other), update frequency as stated, the earliest year of records, and the field name that holds the request closure timestamp.
rubric: 30 fields (6 cities x 5). URLs must be the official portal dataset; field names exact.
